title: Grade 7 French — Mon, Jun 23
description: Pronoms relatifs — Day 1 of 5: 'qui' (subject relative pronoun)
subject: french

questions.question: What is a relative pronoun ('pronom relatif') used for?
options: To ask a question
To link two clauses, replacing a noun and giving more information about it — creating a relative clause
To compare two things
To express time
questions.explanation: Relative pronoun: joins two sentences into one. Example: 'J'ai un chat. Le chat est blanc.' → 'J'ai un chat qui est blanc.' (I have a cat that is white.) 'Qui' replaces 'le chat' (subject of the second clause).

questions.question: 'Qui' is used when the relative pronoun is the ___ of the relative clause.
options: Direct object
Subject — 'qui' replaces a noun that is doing the action in the clause
Indirect object
Location
questions.explanation: 'Qui' = subject relative pronoun. In 'J'ai un ami qui parle français', 'qui' is the subject of 'parle' (he speaks). 'Qui' can refer to people OR things. Never elides: 'qui' stays 'qui' even before a vowel.

questions.question: Join: 'C'est un livre. Le livre est intéressant.' using 'qui'.
options: C'est un livre que est intéressant.
C'est un livre qui est intéressant.
C'est un livre dont est intéressant.
C'est un livre où est intéressant.
questions.explanation: 'C'est un livre qui est intéressant.' ✓ 'Qui' replaces 'le livre' as the subject of 'est intéressant.' Test: 'qui' = the book IS interesting (book = subject of 'est').

questions.question: Fill in: 'Je connais une fille ___ chante très bien.'
options: que
qui
où
dont
questions.explanation: 'Je connais une fille qui chante très bien.' ✓ 'Qui' because 'fille' is the subject of 'chante' (she sings). Test: Can you put 'elle' where the blank is? 'Elle chante très bien' → yes → use 'qui.'

questions.question: The verb in a 'qui' clause agrees with:
options: Always the masculine singular
The noun that 'qui' replaces — the antecedent
The subject of the main clause only
Always the plural
questions.explanation: 'Qui' agrees with its antecedent. Example: 'Ce sont les élèves qui sont intelligents.' (plural, masculine) vs 'C'est la fille qui est intelligente.' (singular, feminine). The verb conjugates for the replaced noun.

questions.question: Translate: 'I have a dog that barks a lot.'
options: J'ai un chien que aboie beaucoup.
J'ai un chien qui aboie beaucoup.
J'ai un chien dont aboie beaucoup.
J'ai un chien aboie beaucoup.
questions.explanation: 'J'ai un chien qui aboie beaucoup.' ✓ 'Chien' = subject of 'aboie' → use 'qui.' 'Que' would be for object. 'Aboyer' = to bark. No elision with 'qui.'

questions.question: Join: 'Voici l'homme. L'homme a trouvé mon sac.'
options: Voici l'homme que a trouvé mon sac.
Voici l'homme qui a trouvé mon sac.
Voici l'homme où a trouvé mon sac.
Voici l'homme dont a trouvé mon sac.
questions.explanation: 'Voici l'homme qui a trouvé mon sac.' ✓ 'L'homme' is the subject of 'a trouvé' → 'qui.' Notice: 'qui' doesn't elide before 'a' (unlike 'que' which becomes 'qu' before a vowel).

questions.question: Spot the error: 'C'est le professeur qu'explique bien.'
options: No error
'qu'' should be 'qui' — 'qui' never elides. 'Que' (not 'qui') elides to 'qu'' before a vowel. Correct: 'C'est le professeur qui explique bien.'
'explique' is wrong
'professeur' needs an article
questions.explanation: 'Qui' NEVER elides — it stays 'qui' even before a vowel: 'qui est,' 'qui aime,' 'qui a.' Only 'que' elides to 'qu'' before a vowel/h-muet. Correct: 'le professeur qui explique bien.'

questions.question: 'Qui' can replace a noun referring to:
options: Only people
Only animals
Both people AND things/animals — 'qui' is not restricted to animate beings
Only abstract nouns
questions.explanation: 'Qui' replaces any noun that is the subject of the relative clause — people, animals, or things. 'J'ai un chat qui dort.' (thing/animal) ✓. 'J'ai une amie qui danse.' (person) ✓.

questions.question: Combine into one sentence: 'Il y a un bus. Ce bus va à l'aéroport.'
options: Il y a un bus qui va à l'aéroport.
Il y a un bus que va à l'aéroport.
Il y a un bus où va à l'aéroport.
Il y a un bus dont va à l'aéroport.
questions.explanation: 'Il y a un bus qui va à l'aéroport.' ✓ 'Bus' = subject of 'va' → 'qui.' 'Aéroport' = airport. The relative clause adds information about the bus.

questions.question: Which TWO relative pronouns can you learn this week? What are their roles?
options: qui and que — both replace subjects
qui (subject) and que (direct object) — key distinction: qui = the noun DOES the action; que = the noun RECEIVES the action
qui and où — both replace people
qui and dont — both replace subjects
questions.explanation: 'Qui' = subject (does the action). 'Que' = direct object (receives the action). This is the most important distinction. 'L'homme qui mange.' (man = subject of eat) vs 'Le repas que je mange.' (meal = object of eat).

questions.question: In 'C'est une ville qui est très belle.' — what does 'qui' refer to?
options: 'C'est' (this)
'ville' (city) — 'qui' replaces 'ville,' which is the subject of 'est très belle'
'belle' (beautiful)
'une' (a)
questions.explanation: The antecedent of 'qui' is 'une ville.' In the relative clause 'qui est très belle,' 'qui' = the city = subject of 'est.' The adjective 'belle' is feminine to agree with 'ville.'

questions.question: Translate: 'She is the student who won the prize.'
options: C'est l'élève que a gagné le prix.
C'est l'élève qui a gagné le prix.
C'est l'élève où a gagné le prix.
C'est l'élève dont a gagné le prix.
questions.explanation: 'C'est l'élève qui a gagné le prix.' ✓ 'L'élève' = subject of 'a gagné' → 'qui.' Passé composé: 'a gagné' (has won). 'Le prix' = the prize.

questions.question: The relative clause in 'J'ai vu le film qui était très long.' tells us:
options: Where the film was seen
What the film was like — it adds descriptive information about 'le film' (that it was very long)
When the film was seen
Who the film was about
questions.explanation: 'Qui était très long' = relative clause that describes 'le film.' It answers: what kind of film? A very long one. This is the key function of relative clauses: to add information (define or describe) the noun.

questions.question: In 'Les enfants qui jouent dans le jardin sont mes cousins.' — 'qui' refers to 'les enfants' which is:
options: Singular
Plural — so the verb 'jouent' is conjugated in the plural (3rd person plural)
Feminine singular
Masculine singular
questions.explanation: 'Les enfants' = masculine plural. 'Qui' replaces 'les enfants' → verb 'jouent' = 3rd person plural (they play). 'Sont mes cousins' = are my cousins (main clause). The relative clause 'qui jouent...' identifies which children.
